title: Compound interest and the Rule of 72
publisher: Artha Kavach summary of public guidance (RBI / SEBI / IRDAI / Income Tax Dept) — pending manual verification
text: Compounding means earning returns on your earlier returns, so growth accelerates with time. At 12% a year, money doubles roughly every 6 years, and at 8% every 9 years — this is the Rule of 72: divide 72 by the annual return to estimate the doubling time in years. Starting early matters more than investing more: someone who invests ₹5,000 a month from age 22 can end up with far more at 60 than someone who invests ₹10,000 a month from age 35, at the same return. The same maths works against you on debt: card interest at 36–48% compounds quickly. These are illustrations, not promises; actual market returns vary and are never guaranteed.
summary_hinglish: Compounding mein return par bhi return milta hai. Rule of 72: 72 ko saalana return se divide karo to paisa double hone ka time pata chalta hai (12% par ~6 saal). Jaldi shuru karna zyada invest karne se bhi zyada matter karta hai. Ye example hain, guarantee nahi.
summary_hi: चक्रवृद्धि में रिटर्न पर भी रिटर्न मिलता है। रूल ऑफ 72: 72 को सालाना रिटर्न से भाग दें तो पैसा दोगुना होने का समय मिलता है (12% पर लगभग 6 साल)। जल्दी शुरू करना ज़्यादा निवेश करने से भी ज़्यादा मायने रखता है। ये उदाहरण हैं, गारंटी नहीं।
